requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST report the number
of nodes without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, except items inside a module
named `tests`, using the following summary:

```text
N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them.
```

The summary MUST report zero when no nodes have warnings. Default output MUST
NOT list individual coverage warnings or coverage-history details, including
with `status --all` or `status --verbose`.
`habeas status --coverage` MUST list every warning, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, and report incomplete coverage history when applicable.
A warning MUST NOT fail validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read
Git history.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate. Each obligation in `requirements.references.coverage.report` maps to at least one marked test with assertions on the outcome. I did not request implementation source.

- **Summary line in `status`, with the count.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` asserts the "N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them." form with a concrete count.
  - `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form]` asserts the same form with a different count.
- **Summary reports zero.** `tests/coverage.rs#fn[incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about]` asserts the summary with a count of zero.
- **Summary from `habeas author` after it finishes.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_only_the_coverage_warning_count_on_stderr]` asserts the count on stderr and no individual warnings.
  - The `tests/authoring_batch.rs` tests assert the summary after a batch, after a `--stdout` run, and after current records are skipped. The `--stdout` test also checks that stdout holds only the record.
  - The authoring tests cover finishing a batch, finishing a single named run, and finishing with nothing assessed.
- **Default output lists no individual warnings or history details, including with `--all` and `--verbose`.**
  - `status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` runs every combination of `--all` and `--verbose`, with and without a selection. It asserts that "has no recent coverage" and the "## Coverage warnings" heading are absent when `--coverage` is not given.
  - The same coverage tests, plus the `author` tests, assert that "history is incomplete" is absent from default output, including in a shallow clone.
- **`status --coverage` lists warnings with file, line, kind and name.** The assertions check the form "<file>:<line>: function <name> has no recent coverage…". They also check that a covered item (`parse`) is not listed.
- **`status --coverage` reports incomplete history.**
  - `status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete` asserts "Coverage history is incomplete" in a depth-1 clone.
  - `incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about` asserts it even when there are no warnings.
  - The same tests assert it is absent in a full repository.
- **Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about]` covers out-of-line `tests.rs` and `tests/mod.rs`.
  - `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module]` covers positive and negative path classification.
  - `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_test_without_a_test_reference_is_an_error_not_a_coverage_warning]` shows a bare `#[test]` is an error while the helper is warned.
  - The `fixture` helper in `mod tests` in `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` is also not warned about.
- **A warning does not fail validation.** `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` asserts `validate_repository` has no coverage error for `parse` after it warns. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones]` asserts validation has no errors while warnings exist.
- **Validation does not read Git history.** `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` deletes the object database. It asserts validation output is unchanged, while `coverage_warnings` reports incomplete history.
- **Examples.** The `coverage.reauthored`, `coverage.new_function` and `coverage.test_module` examples are exercised by `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item`. In it, `parse` is not warned after 2 and 3 reauthorings but is warned afterwards, and `helper` is warned at once.

I found no unaddressed obligation or boundary.

:::{req} coverage.history
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
`habeas status --coverage` MUST say that coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status --coverage` does not warn.
After a third such commit, no version in the window names it, and
`habeas status --coverage` warns about `parse`.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status --coverage` warns about it at once; nothing in any window
names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status --coverage` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the
same module without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
